issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) require addGuestStudents(int, String) — i.e., a method that accepts an int and a String reason — but the solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This mismatch could confuse students (who are instructed to implement the two-parameter method) and makes the solution inconsistent with the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's addGuestStudents method match the specified signature: change its declaration to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update the method body to add the new guests to numberOfGuestStudents (and optionally record or log the reason). Alternatively, adjust the problem statement/UML to accept a single-parameter signature if the reason is intentionally omitted, but keep the API consistent across all artifacts.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) that accepts a number of new guest students and a reason (String). The solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) without the String reason parameter. This signature mismatch breaks the direct mapping between the specified requirement and the reference implementation and may confuse students about the required method signature and its intended use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/UML by changing the solution method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and (optionally) use or store the reason. Alternatively, if the reason parameter is not needed, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) so all artifacts match.
